newsitem.title: MEXICO: Accused Mexican rebels expand hunger strike.
newsitem.headline: Accused Mexican rebels expand hunger strike.

text.p: Six prisoners accused of belonging to a leftist rebel army in the southern Mexican state of Guerrero have joined a widening hunger strike to press for their release, colleagues said on Sunday.

The six peasants, seized in the immediate aftermath of the appearance of the so-called Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) on June 28, said they were joining 12 accused EPR prisoners held in the neighbouring state of Oaxaca in the protest fast.

"We are joining this national hunger strike movement to call attention of political parties, so that they press for our freedom," said Hilario Mesino Acosta, an inmate in the Acapulco prison who also heads the powerful Peasant Organisation in the Southern Mountains (OCSS).

Mesino, who was acting as spokesman for the hunger strikers and was not taking part in the fast, said the men -- including other OCSS members -- were tortured by army and police interrogators before the trial. He also said the judge failed to listen to their arguments when charging them.
The state government denied the men were tortured.
Mesino said they hoped their fate would be taken up by candidates for mid-term congressional elections in Mexico scheduled for July 6.

On Friday, 12 prisoners jailed near the state capital of Oaxaca state launched a hunger strike -- also demanding their release. They were part of a group of 43 men, mostly Zapotec indians from the Loxicha area of Oaxaca, accused of taking part in EPR attacks in August 1996 in which 15 died.
